He is greater here because one woman came to Solomon, whereas all kingdoms have come to Christ.

As now we, who have believed and continue to believe such things, both see and have seen them fulfilled. [Note: The Remigian manuscript reads, “who believe so many things to be fulfilled and both perceive and see them.”]

The Sibyl also acknowledges this, saying (in Augustine, as cited above):

> And before this Lord the kings will all stand together.

### CHAPTER XXXVII

#### That Kings Also Have Accepted the Yoke of the Law of Christ. The Promise Fulfilled

### 39.

The prophet David says:

“Now understand, O kings; be instructed, all you who judge the earth. Serve the Lord in fear, and rejoice in him with trembling. [Note: The Remigian manuscript supplies the verb “be instructed.”]

And again:

“At the assembling of peoples together, [Note: The older printed editions read “and kingdoms”; the Remigian manuscript, together with the more recent editions, reads “and kings.”] and kings, so that they may serve the Lord” (Ps. 102:23). [Note: The Remigian manuscript adds, “And Solomon also.”]

“Love righteousness, you who judge the earth” (Wis. 1:1).

And again:

Paul also judges that one should pray for kings [Note: The Remigian manuscript reads, “he considered it right.”] and for those who are in positions of authority, so that we may lead a quiet and peaceful life (1 Tim. 2:2).

### CHAPTER XXXVIII

[Note: The Remigian manuscript reads, “At the overthrow.”]

#### On the Overthrow of Idols and Temples. The Promise Fulfilled

### 40.

In his law the Lord says through Moses:

“You shall overthrow their altars, cut down their sacred groves, and burn their carved images with fire” (Deut. 7:5; 12:3). [Note: The Remigian manuscript reads, “you shall burn their sacred groves.”]

And the prophet Isaiah:

“All the works made by human hands in Egypt will flee” (Isa. 19:1).

Likewise, he himself says:

“They will hide their gods in caves and in the caverns of rocks, nor will they conceal them there” (Isa. 2:19, according to the Septuagint). [Note: According to the Septuagint version, this passage from Isaiah is reported in such a way that the latter part—“nor will they conceal them there”—expresses the sense of that version more than its wording.]

“May the gods who did not make heaven and earth perish from beneath heaven and earth” (Jer. 10:11). [Note: The Remigian manuscript reads, “from heaven.”]

And through Zechariah the Lord says:

“All the gods are demons” [Note: The Remigian manuscript adds “of the nations,” absent from the printed editions.] (Ps. 96:5).

The Lord confirms these things in the Gospel of Luke, saying:

“Every kingdom divided against itself will be desolated” (Luke 11:17). [Note: This is how the Remigian manuscript reads. The printed editions have a different punctuation: “Even if Satan…”]

“But if Satan also is divided against himself, how will his kingdom stand? Because you say that I cast out demons by Beelzebul. But if I cast out demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons cast them out? Therefore they will be your judges” (Matt. 12:25).

Paul also bears witness, saying:

“We know that an idol is nothing in this world, [Note: The Remigian manuscript reads, “that there is no idol in the world.”] and that there is no God except one” (1 Cor. 8:4).

The Sibyl also acknowledges this (as cited above):

> The men will reject the images, and all their treasure as well.

### 41.

We therefore believe many of these things that were spoken about Christ and accomplished in Christ—things that the people before us believed when they saw them, and that we see being fulfilled.

To say something about our own times: under the reign of Constantine, the Christian emperor, the Donatist schism was refuted by his judgment [Note: Thus the Remigian manuscript reads; the printed editions have “by his decision”], and Arius was punished by divine authority.

Under the rule of the devout emperor Theodosius, when all the temples were closed and stripped of their vain images by the counts Jovius and Gaudentius [Note: Restored from the Remigian manuscript. The printed editions formerly read, “all temples stripped,” omitting the reference to the images], who among us is permitted not to know this?

Symmachus, that man endowed with marvelous eloquence and learning, yet a pagan, informed the Christian emperor, whom he knew to be such, through a speech of praise delivered in the imperial consistory, using the subtle skill at his disposal, that the Altar of Victory should be restored in the Senate.

The emperor immediately expelled him from his presence and ordered him, at the hundredth milestone, to remain there, placed upon an unprepared cart.

Eutropius also, a very powerful patrician [Note: Thus the Remigian manuscript reads. The printed editions have “very greatly,” omitting “in spirit and mind.”] and pagan in spirit and mind, had secretly caused an edict to be engraved by the Christian emperor Arcadius, to the insult of the Church, decreeing that if anyone fled to her for refuge, he would be removed even from the altar and suffer greater penalties.

By divine judgment, he himself was the first to receive the penalty of his own decree. Having incurred the displeasure of the aforesaid ruler, he fled for refuge to the one whose Church he hated. That holy mother received her enemy into the bosom of her compassion.

Through the venerable priest John, she obtained pardon for him and granted life and safety to the hateful and proud man. [Note: The Remigian manuscript reads, “to the mocking man.”] By his example she warned all enemies that it is useless for them to kick against the goad (Acts 9:5).

Honorius also, the younger son of Theodosius, endowed with Christian religion and devotion, granted all the temples, together with the spaces adjoining them, to the Churches, and likewise gave authority for their images to be shattered.

### 42.

What was accomplished under that same emperor [Note: The Remigian manuscript reads, “under the same man.”] in fulfillment of this promise of God I shall recount briefly and from memory, as divine grace assists my recollection, in two or three instances. [Note: The Remigian manuscript reads, “recounting them.”]

At Alexandria, in the temple of Serapis, this was an example of demonic deception. An iron chariot, supported by no base and fastened to the walls by no hooks, hung suspended in the air, presenting to mortal eyes a source of astonishment and what seemed like divine assistance.

Yet a magnet stone, fixed in the ceiling, supported the entire machine by suspending the iron attached to it. [Note: Later editions read “drawn to it.”]

When a certain servant of God, inspired, understood this, he immediately removed the magnet from the ceiling. The entire spectacle fell, broke, and was shattered, showing that what a mortal human being had supported [Note: The Remigian manuscript reads, “had fashioned”] was not divine.

### 43.

Near the city of Rome there was a certain cavern in which a dragon of extraordinary size had been fashioned by mechanical art. It carried a sword in its mouth, its eyes glittered with gems, and it appeared frightening and terrifying.

Each year devoted maidens, adorned with flowers, were offered to it in sacrifice [Note: The editions of Cologne and later read, “as a sacrifice”], in such a manner that, while unknowingly bringing the offerings and touching the step of the ladder from which that dragon, by the devil’s art, was suspended [Note: Thus the Remigian manuscript reads. The printed editions have, “from which the whole thing hung by that art of the devil”], the force of the descending sword would strike them down, so that innocent blood might be shed.

A certain monk, well known for his merit, overturned this arrangement in the presence of Stilicho, who was then a patrician, in the following way. Feeling each step with his staff and inspecting it, as soon as he touched it and discovered the devilish deception [Note: The printed editions read, “examined it”], he descended after crossing it, cut the dragon apart, and divided it into pieces, showing here also that gods made by hand are not gods.

### 44.

At Carthage in Africa, they claimed that there was a temple of Caelestis, extremely large and surrounded by buildings of all their gods. Its paved square, decorated with mosaic pavement, precious columns, and walls, extended for nearly two thousand paces. [Note: The Remigian manuscript reads, “with a mosaic pavement.”]

After it had long remained closed and neglect had buried it beneath thorny growth, when the Christian people wished to claim it for the use of the true religion, the pagan population loudly asserted that dragons and asps were there to guard the temple. [Note: The Remigian manuscript reads, “dragons … to guard their temple.”]

The Christians, fired all the more by zeal, removed all these obstacles without injury, so that they might consecrate the temple to their true heavenly King and Lord.

For when the solemn festival of Easter was being celebrated, a multitude gathered there, including priests arriving from every direction with the greatest curiosity. Aurelius, the father and bishop worthy of remembrance, already a citizen of the heavenly homeland, both established his chair there in place of Caelestis and sat upon it.

I myself was present then with companions and friends. And while, as is natural for the impatient age of youth, we looked around and inspected each detail according to the building’s grandeur, something strange and unbelievable presented itself to our eyes: an inscription written in larger bronze letters on the front of the temple:

> AURELIUS THE PONTIFF DEDICATED THIS.

The people marveled as they read it.

The events had then been accomplished by a prophetic spirit, which the foreknowing order of God had brought to this definite conclusion.

When a pagan produced a false prophecy, supposedly belonging to that same Caelestis, saying that roads and temples would once again be restored to their ancient rites, the true God—he, I say, the true God, whose prophetic predictions know absolutely neither how to lie nor how to deceive—under Constantius and the Augusta Placidia, whose son Valentinian, now devout and Christian, is emperor [Note: Restored from the Remigian manuscript. The printed editions all previously read “Valentinus.”], with the tribune Ursus in command, brought all those temples down to their foundations. He left the land for the burial, evidently, of the dead; and the Vandal hand has now overturned the road itself, leaving no memory of it.

### 45.

I myself also know that in a certain part of the province of Mauretania, images of great antiquity had been brought out from caves and caverns in such a way that the whole city, together with its clergy, was bound in the sacrilege of perjury.

What was done throughout the other provinces in this matter is known to everyone, and the outcomes themselves demonstrate it.

That future grieved Hermes Trismegistus, and in mourning he wrote, among other things:

> “Then this land, the most holy seat of shrines and temples, will become exceedingly full of the bodies and corpses of the dead.”

But the Spirit of God foretold it beforehand; even the spirits of demons were unable to remain silent while confessing it, especially those who themselves had said to the Lord:

“Why have you come before the time to destroy us?” (Mark 1:24). [Note: The Remigian manuscript reads, “to torture us.”]

Here was that great multitude of certain and uncertain gods whom Varro records; here also were those eminent and chosen gods, together with their king Jupiter, hurling thunderbolts, formidable in counsel and power—as their worshipers claim—and terrifying in arms.

Here, here, they ought to have done something, if not for the world, at least for themselves, so that one Crucified Man would not destroy them. But they perished, as we know, and the prophet David confirms it, saying:

“Their memory has perished with a crash, but the Lord remains forever” (Ps. 9:8).

### CHAPTER XXXIX

[Note: The Remigian manuscript adds, “and the poor.”]

#### That Kings, People of Moderate Means, and the Poor Will Come Together Equally at the One Table of Christ. The Promise Fulfilled

### 46.

The prophet Isaiah says:

“Then,” he says, “the wolf will feed together with the lamb, the leopard will rest beside the kid, and the ox, lion, and lamb will eat straw together, and a little child will feed them” (Isa. 11:6).

And David says:

“For behold, the kings of the earth were gathered and came together; when they saw this, they were astonished” (Ps. 48:5–6).

Likewise he himself:

“Who is like the Lord our God, who dwells on high and regards the lowly? He raises the needy from the earth and lifts the poor from the dungheap, to place him with princes, with the princes of his people” (Ps. 113:5 and following).

Solomon also says:

“He himself made both the small and the great, and he cares equally for all” (Wis. 6:8).

And again:

“Wisdom,” he says, “built herself a house and set up seven pillars. She slaughtered her sacrifices [Note: The Remigian manuscript reads, “her victims”], mixed her wine in a bowl, and prepared her table. She sent out her servants, calling and saying: ‘Come, eat of my bread and drink the wine that I have mixed for you’” (Prov. 9:1 and following).

The Lord confirms these things in the Gospel, at that supper which the great and wealthy man himself prepared for his son.

“He sent servants,” he says, “so that those who had been invited might come, but they excused themselves in this way. One said: ‘I have bought a farm, and I must go to see it; please consider me excused.’ Another said: ‘I have bought five yoke of oxen.’ Another said: ‘I have taken a wife’” (Luke 14:16 and following). [Note: The Remigian manuscript reads, “and therefore I cannot come,” and adds “and another.”]

In these three excuses are the desire of the flesh, the desire of the eyes, and worldly ambition (1 John 2:16). Held back by these things, the Jews, who had been invited to the supper of Christ, refused to come.

“Go,” said the master of the house, “through the squares and streets, and bring in those whom you find” (Matt. 22:9).

From these, the Gentiles were brought in.

“There is still room,” he said. “Go,” he says, “along the hedges and roads, and compel those whom you find to enter” (Luke 14:22–23).

From these he brings in the rich, kings, and certain heretics—those whom he has outside his fold—compelled to come. [Note: The Remigian manuscript reads, “he will bring them in.”] He is the one who says:

“No one comes to me unless the Father who sent me draws him” (John 6:44).

To those who come he also says:

“He who eats my flesh and drinks my blood has eternal life, and I will raise him up on the last day” (ibid., 55).

Who these people are, the apostle Paul shows:

“There is neither Jew nor Greek; there is neither slave nor free; there is neither male nor female. For you are all one in Christ Jesus” (Gal. 3:28).

The words of the Sibyl that we quoted above also correspond to this chapter, where she says (in Augustine, as cited above):

[Note: In Augustine and in the Remigian manuscript: “He will cast down.” In the printed editions: “He cast down.”]

> He will cast down the hills and raise the valleys from below.  
> There will be nothing lofty or high among human affairs.

In agreement with this, Maro says (Eclogue 4.22):

> Nor will the herds fear the great lions.

### CHAPTER XL

#### That When All the Nations Have Believed, the End Will Come. The Promise Fulfilled

### 47.

The prophet Isaiah says:

“All the islands of the nations will worship him from their places” (Zeph. 2:11). [Note: If the author himself cited Isaiah, this is a lapse of memory. The words themselves are from Zephaniah 2:11 according to the Septuagint.]

And through the prophet Malachi:

“From the rising of the sun to its setting, my name will be glorified among the nations,” says the Lord. [Note: The Remigian manuscript adds, “and David, a sacrifice.”] “And in every place a pure sacrifice will be offered to my name” (Mal. 1:11).

Isaiah likewise:

“For the earth has been filled so that it may know God, as abundant water covers the sea” (Isa. 11:9).

The Lord confirms these things in the Gospel of Matthew, saying:

“And this Gospel will be preached as a testimony to all nations, and then the end will come” (Matt. 24:14).

Through the prophet Haggai these signs were given concerning the end of the world: [Note: The Remigian manuscript reads “Zechariah.” But the first part, “Behold, I … the earth,” contains the words of Haggai 2:7 according to the Septuagint. The second part, “and I will make …,” is Isaiah 13:9.]

“Behold,” says the Lord, “once again I will shake heaven and earth, and I will make the world an empty place, and the cities such that they will not be inhabited” (Hag. 2:7, according to the Septuagint; Isa. 13:9).

And Habakkuk says:

“Destruction will come upon the wicked” (Hab. 1:9, according to the Septuagint).

And again:

“The fig tree,” he says, “will not yield its fruit, and there will be no produce on the vines. The work of the olive will deceive, and the fields will yield no food. The sheep will fail for lack of food; there will be no cattle in the stalls. But I,” he says, “will rejoice in the Lord” (Hab. 3:17 and following). [Note: The Remigian manuscript has this wording. The printed editions read, “will not yield … the things growing in them.”]

The wise men of the world also bore witness to these matters, as in the statement of Sallust:

> “It is necessary that all things which have arisen should perish, and that things which have grown should grow old” (Sallust, Preface to *The Jugurthine War*, near the beginning).

The later Academics also thought that all things tending toward destruction were uncertain. Plato said:

> “If he gave the world a beginning, he also gave it an end.”

Hence another says:

> “What is this? That in which there is something final.”

[Note: The Remigian manuscript reads, “and Cicero.” In fact, Cicero says in *On Old Age* 69: “What is long in human life? But to me nothing seems even long-lasting if it has something final.”]

The Lord himself confirms these things by giving signs of everything that is to come.

“When you see all these things happening,” he says, “know that the end is near” (Matt. 24:33). [Note: This is how it is read in the Remigian manuscript. The printed editions omit the two words “he says … happening.”]

The apostle John also says:

“The world will pass away, and its desire” (1 John 2:17).

The things destined for the end, during the half of the time that follows, will be demonstrated in the chapters that follow, joined together: so that we may conclude this third period, like a third day, rising from the four evangelists as from the hinges of the world, with the eastern ray passing away with the evangelist John, and Matthew, Mark, and Luke occupying the three divisions, and with the number of the twelve disciples corresponding also to the number of the hours.

Thus may the very day on which he rose from the dead, when it comes eternal in majesty, make us eternal, living with him, and always grant us to praise God without end. [Note: The Remigian manuscript reads “to find,” perhaps “to be found.”]

## PART FOUR

[Note: In the Remigian manuscript the following work is summarized as: “Here begins, under grace, the half of the time, concerning the signs of Antichrist.”]

### THE HALF OF THE TIME, AT WHOSE END THE VISIONS MADE IN THE HOLY SCRIPTURES CONCERNING ANTICHRIST ARE TO BE FULFILLED

## PROLOGUE

### 1.

In this half of the time—the end of the world and the signs that are to come, as well as the deeds of Antichrist himself, his pride, and his power for a brief time—we have undertaken, with the Lord granting and his grace effecting it, to prove these matters by chapters drawn from divine testimonies.

First, however, I shall briefly set forth and demonstrate what he was who is now called the devil, and in what manner he was formed by the author of all good things; then also his fall, ruin, and end, drawing briefly upon every authority of prophecy and the New Testament, so that it may not be burdensome if everything is included in this work. [Note: The Remigian manuscript reads, “to be briefly made known.”]

## CHAPTER I

#### How the Angel Who Through Pride Became the Devil Was Created

[Note: In the Remigian manuscript: “The fulfilled prediction concerning how he was created”; and similarly in the titles of the other chapters.]

#### The Prediction Fulfilled

### 2.

Through Ezekiel the Lord speaks concerning him:

“You were the seal of likeness, full of wisdom and perfect in beauty; you were in the paradise of your God. Every precious stone was your covering; you walked in the midst of stones of fire, perfect in your ways from the day of your creation, until iniquity was found in you” (Ezek. 28:12 and following).

And Isaiah:

“How,” he says, “has Lucifer fallen, he who was rising at dawn?” (Isa. 14:12).

The Lord confirms these things in the Gospel:

“You are from your father the devil,” he says to the Jews. “He was a murderer from the beginning and did not stand in the truth” (John 8:44).

He was made in the truth in which he did not stand, because he refused to be subject to the Creator, whose power even in his wickedness he did not escape. [Note: The Remigian manuscript adds here, “from the truth.”]

## CHAPTER II

#### With What Pride the Devil Fell

#### The Prediction Fulfilled

### 3.

The prophet Isaiah speaks concerning him:

“You said in your heart: ‘I will ascend into heaven; above the stars of God I will exalt my throne; I will sit on the mountain of the covenant, on the sides of the north. I will ascend above the heights of the clouds, and I will be like the Most High’” (Isa. 14:13–14). [Note: Thus the Remigian manuscript reads. The printed editions have, “He was saying … in his heart.”]

And in Ezekiel:

“Your heart was lifted up in your beauty,” he says; “you destroyed all wisdom” (Ezek. 28:17). [Note: The Remigian manuscript reads, “you destroyed your wisdom.”]

The Lord confirms these things in the Gospel:

“Now,” he says, “is the judgment of the world; now the prince of this world has been cast down” (John 12:31). [Note: The supplied citation reads “John XII, 13,” but the quotation corresponds to John 12:31.]

The apostle Peter also bears witness in his epistle to the nations:

“For God did not spare the angels when they sinned” (2 Pet. 2:4).

Yet he spares sinful human beings, because a human being sinned when the devil deceived him, whereas the devil deceived himself by sinning.

## CHAPTER III

#### Where the Devil Was Cast Down

#### The Prediction Fulfilled

[Note: The Remigian manuscript adds here, “believed only.”]

### 4.

The prophet Isaiah says:

“Nevertheless, you will be brought down to the underworld, to the depth of the pit” (Isa. 14:15).

And shortly afterward:

“But you have been cast out from your tomb, like a useless shoot” (ibid., 19). [Note: The Remigian manuscript adds, “polluted and wrapped up,” and contains no more of the prophetic passage.]

And through Ezekiel the Lord speaks concerning him:

“I cast you to the earth; I placed you before the faces of kings, so that they might see you and the multitude of your iniquities. And by the iniquity of your commerce you destroyed your sanctification” (Ezek. 28:17–18).

The Lord confirms these things in the Gospel, saying:

“I was watching Satan fall from heaven like lightning” (Luke 10:18).

For he fell still further when Jesus allowed himself to be tempted by him, displaying the wickedness of his deception and teaching his own followers how they ought to resist the tempter (Matt. 4:1). [Note: All the printed editions read “to tempt”; this is plainly an error, which the Remigian manuscript does not correct.]

The apostle Peter also says:

“He handed them over, having thrust them into the prisons of darkness of the underworld, to be kept for punishment at the judgment” (1 Pet. 2:4).

And in the Apocalypse of John it is said:

“That great dragon was cast down, that ancient serpent who is called the devil and Satan, who deceives the whole world; he was cast down to the earth, and his angels were cast down with him” (Rev. 12:9 and following), following his ruinous pride.

A “woe” was pronounced upon the earth and the sea:

“Because the devil has come down to you, having great anger, knowing that he has little time for his work of deception” (ibid., 12). [Note: The Remigian manuscript reads, “in his work.”]

What he did in deceiving the proud and the greedy is contained in the earlier parts of this book. Now, briefly—that is, at the end of time—we shall set forth what his deceptions will be, with the signs preceding them, as has been said.

## CHAPTER IV

#### On the Devil Bound and Sent into the Abyss

#### The Prediction Fulfilled

[Note: The Remigian manuscript adds here, “believed only,” and omits the words “and sent into the abyss.”]

5. The prophet David says: “The dragon whom you fashioned to mock him” (Ps. CIII, 26). And again: “You crushed the heads of dragons upon the waters; you broke the head of the great dragon and gave him as food to the Ethiopian peoples” (Ps. LXXIII, 13–14). And in the Book of Job it is said: “This is the beginning of the Lord’s creature, which he made to be mocked by his angels” (Job XL, 14).

[Note: [Col. 0839D] The Remigius manuscript adds here “John.” But what is cited here is read in Luke, nowhere in John.]

The Evangelist confirms this, saying: “The demons begged Jesus not to send them into the abyss” (Luke VIII, 31). And elsewhere Jesus said to his disciples: “Behold, I have given you power to tread upon serpents and scorpions, and [Note: [Col. 0839D] The Remigius manuscript reads *non vos* (“not you”), rather than *non vobis* (“to/for you”).] they will not harm you” (Luke X, 19). Likewise the Lord says: “No one enters the house of a strong man to plunder the vessels of his house unless he first binds the strong man” (Matt. XII, 19).

Beyond these testimonies, the Apocalypse of John bears witness: “I saw an angel [Col. 0839D] descending from heaven, holding [Note: [Col. 0839D] We emend this from the Remigius manuscript. The printed editions have “a throne.”] a great chain in [Col. 0840A] his hand; and he seized that great dragon, that ancient serpent, who is called the devil and Satan, and bound him for a thousand years, and cast him into the abyss. And he shut it and sealed it over him, so that he might no longer deceive the nations until the thousand years were completed. After this he must be released for a short time” (Rev. XX, 1ff.).

Here he explained what is said in the same book concerning Gog and Magog (ibid., 7), Hebrew words which in Latin are rendered “covered” and “uncovered,” so that we understand “covered” to mean that the devil was cast into the abyss, which was shut and sealed over him; and “uncovered” to mean that he must be released and brought forth for a short time.

6. The thousand years, however, are to be understood either as a part standing for the whole—as the apostle Peter says (2 Pet. III, 8): “For one day with the Lord is like a thousand years, and a thousand years like one day”—or from the issuing of the word, when Daniel determined that seventy weeks would elapse until Christ the Leader (Dan. IX, 25).

For then, it is said, the battle took place, when Michael and his angels fought with the dragon; and the angel showed Daniel, saying that he had been sent to fight against the prince of the kingdom of Persia: “And there is no one,” he said, “who helps me except Michael, your prince” (Dan. X, 13). In that battle the devil was defeated, cast down, and bound, [Note: [Col. 0839D] Thus we read in the Remigius manuscript. This reading seemed to us more conformable to the sacred text cited above than the reading found in the printed editions, “he was defeated and his principality.”] just as it was shown to that same prophet at the beginning, and to John at the end of time. [Note: [Col. 0840D] The Remigius manuscript has “as it was shown to the prophet at the beginning.”]

Thus those four hundred and ninety years, and the years that have elapsed from the Savior’s advent until the release of that same devil, [Note: [Col. 0840D] The older printed editions unanimously read “solitude.” The Remigius manuscript and more recent editions read “release.” The latter is certainly better, since it refers to what is read above from Apocalypse XX, 3: “After this he must be released for a short time.”] comprise the thousand years during which the devil was bound, so that he might no longer deceive the nations whom he had previously possessed through idolatries. [Note: [Col. 0840D] The Remigius manuscript has: “are enclosed within a thousand years … whom he had previously deceived.”]

Yet with what power, as the blessed Augustine of venerable memory says (*The City of God*, book XX, chapter 7, §2), will the saints then prevail, who will have to struggle with the released devil, when so many dangers are endured in fighting him while he is bound? For already, as Paul says, “the mystery of lawlessness is at work” (2 Thess. II, 7). But what his mysteries are, with the Lord’s help, will be set forth in the chapters appended below.

## CHAPTER V

[Note: [Col. 0840D] The Remigius manuscript has: “The promise fulfilled, by which the devil works mysteries through all his followers: believed and witnessed by us.”]

How the devil works the mysteries of iniquity through all his followers. The prophecy fulfilled.

[Col. 0840C]

7. The Apocalypse of John says: “The beast was seized, together with the false prophet who had performed signs, by which signs he deceived those who received the inscription of the beast on their forehead and on their hand” (Rev. XIX, 20; XIV, 9).

The inscription on the forehead and hand means not merely imitating the devil’s deeds, but also taking pride in his evil works, so that under the figure of Christ they may perform the deeds of Antichrist.

The Lord Jesus also testified concerning them in the Gospel, saying: “Many will come in my name, saying, ‘I am Christ,’ and they will deceive many; do not go after them” (Mark XIII, 6). And the apostle John says: “You have heard that the Antichrist is coming; now many Antichrists have arisen” (1 John II, 18). And he shows who these are: “They went out from us, but they were not of us. For if they had been of us, they would certainly have remained with us” (ibid., 19).

He indicates all heretics, and especially the Arians, whom we now see deceiving many, whether by temporal power, by the ingenuity of an evil intellect, or certainly by ascetic frugality, or by deception through whatever signs. The Apostle says: “For Satan himself transforms himself into an angel of light. It is therefore no great thing if his ministers also transform themselves as ministers of righteousness; their end will be according to their works” (2 Cor. XI, 14–15). The Lord will say to those who boast of their miracles: “I do not know you. Depart from me, all you who work iniquity” (Matt. VII, 23; Ps. VI, 9).

[Note: [Col. 0841D] We supply from the Remigius manuscript the words “For iniquity is the rending of unity.” They were absent from all the printed editions.]

For iniquity is the rending of unity, as though one were tearing the garment of Christ, or the nets of the apostles who fish for men. [Note: [Col. 0841D] The Lugdunense edition notes in the margin: “Above he used ‘garment’ metaphorically for the Church; here he uses ‘nets’ metaphorically—*μεταφορικῶς*, ‘figuratively’—for evangelical teaching, by which the apostles, as it were, fish for human beings.”]

All heretics are found alienated from their fellowship. They have abandoned the peace of communion and the bread of God and of the apostles, and preach in their own places—not in churches but in the streets. They do not share in their memorials; separated from the whole, they assume the Catholic name for themselves.

Yet in Jerusalem itself James and Stephen, the first martyr; John at Ephesus; Andrew and the others throughout Asia; and the apostles Peter and Paul in the city of Rome consecrated by their blood and memorials the Church of the nations—in which they instructed people in the teaching of Christ the Lord—handing down to posterity one peaceful and united Church.

The Christian who shares communion with this universal Church is [Note: [Col. 0841D] The Remigius manuscript adds “and Catholic.”] Catholic. One who is separated from it is a heretic and an Antichrist. When he has been openly revealed, the following passages will show that he will perform greater signs.

## CHAPTER VI

Concerning the signs of Antichrist. The prophecy fulfilled.

[Note: [Col. 0841D] The Remigius manuscript has: “Concerning the signs of Antichrist, believed and witnessed by us.”]

8. In the Book of Job it is said concerning Antichrist: “His strength is in his loins, and his power is upon the navel of his belly” (Job XL, 1). And again: “There is no power upon earth that can be compared with him who was made so as to fear nothing. He sees every lofty thing; he is king over all the sons of pride” (Job XLI, 24–25). [Col. 0841C]

The apostle Paul also says: “According to the working of Satan, with every power, signs, and lying wonders, and with every deception of iniquity for those who are perishing” (2 Thess. II, 9–10). And the Lord says in the Gospel: “False Christs and false prophets will arise, and they will give great signs and wonders, so as to deceive, if it were possible, even the elect. Behold, I have foretold it to you” (Matt. XXIV, 24–25).

Although the apostle Paul also tacitly mentions some who have a seared conscience (1 Tim. IV, 2), he speaks openly of others, such as Hymenaeus and Philetus, Demas, Hermogenes, and Alexander the coppersmith, whose errors, varied teachings, and many evils he recalls (2 Tim. II, 17; IV, 9; I, 15; IV, 14; Acts XX, 29). He himself testifies that after his departure grievous wolves would not be lacking, and that the one who even now works in the children of disobedience would come (Eph. II, 2).

9. In our own times, when Aspar, consul for the sixth time, had been appointed at Carthage, who among the citizens of that region is unaware of the diabolical and monstrous sign that occurred there? [Note: [Col. 0841D] From this passage, which indicates that the event occurred when Aspar was established at Carthage as consul for the sixth time, it is easy to believe that Aspar held the consulship six times. Yet a very learned man argues that this conflicts with the Consular Fasti. He therefore reasonably suspects that one should instead read *V. C.*, “Most Distinguished Man,” or *V. I. cons.*, “Illustrious Man, consul,” which would fall in the year 434. Nevertheless, he thinks it difficult to grant that Aspar was at that time at Carthage.]

A certain young woman, Arab by nationality and a slave by status, wearing the appearance of a servant of God, while bathing and shamelessly gazing upon a certain image of Venus and upon herself, comparing herself to it, offered herself as a dwelling place to the devil. [Note: [Col. 0842D] The Remigius manuscript reads: “While she was bathing and, looking upon a certain image of Venus in the boy, … offered herself as a dwelling place to the devil; immediately he …”]

Immediately that lion “who prowls around roaring” (1 Pet. V, 8) found the prey he was seeking. Taking possession of her throat, so that she could pass through neither food nor drink for nearly seventy days and as many nights, the devil displayed his fast from the vessel he had seized and possessed. [Note: [Col. 0842D] The Lugdunense, Lovaniense, Duacense, and Cologne editions read “from the vessel seized and possessed.” More recent editions read “from the vessel seized.” The Remigius manuscript reads “from the vessel desired and possessed.”]

The girl’s parents, hoping that the monster could be removed after so many days, could no longer endure the continuing evil. Together with their daughter they presented themselves to a priest, faithfully explaining what had happened. The girl admitted only this: that in the middle of the night a certain bird appeared and poured something into her mouth.

Everyone was then astonished to see that the girl bore no marks of prolonged fasting and was not disfigured by pallor, wasting, or weakness; rather, she was robust in the vigor of her organs and the size of her limbs. [Note: [Col. 0842D] The Remigius manuscript has “by prolonged fasting.”]

Since the reported events seemed unbelievable, after deliberation the priest [confined] the girl in a monastery of women where the relics of Saint Stephen are kept, and entrusted her to the superior. [Note: [Col. 0842D] We believe that the word “confined,” or another word of the same meaning, must be supplied here.]

There she said that the bird had appeared only on the first day and had reproached her because she had not been driven by hunger or thirst to seek that place, which it was not permitted to approach. She remained in the monastery for two full weeks without taking any food or drink.

10. It happened that the fifteenth Sunday dawned. When the priest went up with us so that the morning sacrifice might customarily be offered there, the superior led the girl to the altar, walking and dressed as women usually do when they arrive flushed from eating and drinking.

But when she threw herself down before the altar, her cries and weeping brought groans and tears from all who were present; through them the assembled people implored the Lord to remove so great an evil. [Note: [Col. 0842D] The Remigius manuscript reads “provoked.”] For there was already an unseemly murmur among the people.

When the sacrifice had been completed, the girl received from the priest, along with the others, a small portion of the body of the Lord, anointed. Although she chewed it into small pieces, she could not swallow it, because the one of whom the Apostle says had not yet been driven out: “What harmony is there between Christ and Belial?” (2 Cor. VI, 15). And again: “You cannot drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons. You cannot partake of the table of the Lord and the table of demons” (1 Cor. X, 20–21).

The priest therefore supported her face with his hand so that she would not spit out the holy sacrament. One of the deacons suggested that the bishop apply the cup of salvation to her throat. When this was done, as soon as the devil, by the Savior’s command, left the place that he had occupied, the girl cried out, praising the Redeemer, that she had swallowed the sacrament she was holding in her mouth.

Then there was joy; then voices rose in glory to God, because, after eighty-five days, once the devil had been expelled, the girl had been rescued from the power of the enemy. [Note: [Col. 0842D] This number is indicated by the Remigius manuscript, which results from the seventy and fifteen days of the girl’s fast mentioned above. All the printed editions read “eighty-two”; it would not have been difficult for scribes to turn LXXXV into LXXXII.]

An offering of thanksgiving was again made for her, and after receiving a portion of the sacrifice she was restored to her former condition. [Col. 0843A] At that same time, while these things were taking place, a deacon of that title, moved by the divine Spirit, removed that statue and smashed it to dust; and divine majesty overcame all the cunning of the one lying in wait.

11. We also know that someone came there in the guise of a monk, claiming to perform various signs of healing. While he performed certain fanciful tricks upon the blind and lame and anointed them with oil infused with the bone of some dead man—I know not whom—they thought that sight and the power of walking had been restored to them. [Note: [Col. 0843D] Thus the Remigius manuscript. The printed editions read “he anointed them with the bone.”] But when they departed, they remained in the infirmities by which they had previously been held. [Note: [Col. 0843D] The Remigius manuscript reads “when they departed.”] Recognizing that he had been exposed in these matters, that deceiver fled.

12. A devout and noble Christian related that the same man, or another, had performed such deeds in Asia. [Note: [Col. 0843D] Thus the Remigius manuscript. The printed editions read “and to us.”]

In Italy also, while we were staying in Campania, the venerable Pope Leo—who deserves to be named with apostolic honor—was overthrowing the Manichaeans and crushing the Pelagians, especially Julian. At that time a certain man named Florus, seized by a spirit of deception, attributing to himself the power and merit of Saint Sossius the martyr, was making certain promises and committing unlawful acts not far from the city of Naples, to the ruin of souls. He was detained and restrained by the brother of our venerable bishop Nostrianus and by the presbyter Herius, together with the clergy of the aforesaid Church, [Note: [Col. 0843D] The Remigius manuscript adds “deservedly restrained,”] and thus he was deservedly driven from the borders of that province. [Note: [Col. 0843D] The Remigius manuscript reads “by the people of that province.”]

That one who seeks companions for his own destruction performs many deeds throughout various lands. For this reason I have thought it necessary to report a few of his acts in this work, so that those who will come after us may learn by reading with what vigilance, aided by God, they can overcome the enemy.

## CHAPTER VII

Concerning the woman and the beast by which she is carried. The prophecy to be fulfilled.

13. The apostle John says in the Apocalypse: “One of the seven holy angels came and spoke with me, saying: ‘Come, I will show you the judgment of the great prostitute who sits upon many waters.’ And he carried me away in the Spirit, and I saw a woman sitting upon a beast that had seven heads and ten horns, holding in her hand a cup full of abominations, the uncleanness and fornication of the whole earth” (Rev. XVII, 1ff.). And shortly afterward: “I saw that woman drunk with the blood of the saints and with the blood of the martyrs of Christ Jesus” (ibid., 6).

This is that great Babylon, destined to be stripped throughout the world of its trophies; and her daughter is the wretched woman—whoever imitates her deeds and her pride. [Note: [Col. 0843D] The older printed editions and the Remigius manuscript read *Babylonia*; more recent editions read *Babylon*.] Do not think of her as a city in one place, for she is spread throughout the world.

The prophet David also speaks of her: “O wretched daughter of Babylon, blessed is he who repays you with the repayment that you repaid us” (Ps. CXXXVI, 8). And in the Apocalypse of John it is said: “Repay her as she herself repaid you; in the cup in which she mixed for you, mix her a double measure. As much as she glorified herself and exercised power, so much give her torment and mourning.” [Note: [Col. 0843D] The Remigius manuscript reads “powers … mourning.”] For she says: “I sit as queen, and I am not a widow, and I shall see no mourning.” Therefore in one hour her plagues came: death, famine, and mourning. [Col. 0843D] And she herself will be burned with fire, because the Lord who judges her is mighty (Rev. XVIII, 6ff.). [Note: [Col. 0843D] The Remigius manuscript reads: “And they will burn her with fire … who judged her.”]

14. Who does not understand what he means by calling her one who bears a cup full of the abominations of uncleanness and of the fornication of the whole earth? [Note: [Col. 0843D] The Remigius manuscript reads “fornication.”] When she is called eternal, although she is temporal, this is plainly a name and blasphemy: for mortals, even though they are kings, are called gods in her, and suppliants say to them, “To your deity, to your altars, to your eternity,” and so forth. Vanity, not truth, conveys and teaches these things, and they are execrable. [Note: [Col. 0844D] The Lugdunense edition reads “has handed down, and”; the Remigius manuscript reads “has handed down, certainly”; the other manuscripts read “hands down.”] For these honors belong to the eternal God.

Indeed, in sacrilegious rites and through soft or effeminate priests, she invited all nations to the fornication of idolatry and defiled herself in her subjects. Concerning them the sacred Psalm cries out: “You destroyed all who fornicate away from you” (Ps. LXXII, 27).

Nevertheless, because there are citizens of the heavenly homeland, Jerusalem, within her, who say, “But for me it is good to cling to God” (ibid., 28), they are told: “Come out of her, my people, so that you may not share in her sins and may not be struck by her plagues” (Rev. XVIII, 1).

Those who come out are the ones who follow not her arrogance [Note: [Col. 0844D] The Remigius manuscript reads “so that her arrogance does not …”] but Christ, the humble way; who love not plunder but mercy; who preserve peace and holiness (Heb. XII, 14), without which no one will be able to see God; who groan and grieve over the iniquities committed in their midst (Ezek. IX, 4); and who do not bear the yoke together with unbelievers (2 Cor. VI, 14).

The Lord also exhorts them in the Gospel with his own address, saying among other things: “Blessed are the meek, for they shall possess the earth. Blessed are the merciful, for they shall obtain mercy. Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called sons of God. Blessed are those who mourn, for they shall be comforted. Blessed are those who suffer persecution for righteousness’ sake, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven” (Matt. V, 4ff.).

Paul also testifies, saying: “Let the one who now restrains continue to restrain, until he is taken out of the midst; and then the lawless one will be revealed, whom the Lord Jesus will kill with the breath of his mouth” (2 Thess. II, 7ff.), “and will destroy by the brightness of his coming” (Isa. XI, 4).

## CHAPTER VIII

Concerning the ten kings whom Antichrist will find. The promise to be fulfilled.

[Note: [Col. 0844D] The Remigius manuscript reads “to be fulfilled”; the printed editions read “fulfilled.”]

15. In the Apocalypse John says that the angel told him: “Why are you astonished? I will tell you the mystery of this woman and of the beast by which she is carried. The beast that you saw was and is not, but it is about to rise from the abyss and go into destruction. Its seven heads are seven mountains upon which the woman sits; and they are seven kings: five have fallen, one is, the other has not yet come, and when he comes he must remain for a short time. The beast that was and is not is itself the eighth, although it is one of the seven, and it will go into destruction. And the ten horns that you saw are ten kings; these have not yet received a kingdom, but they will receive royal authority for one hour after the beast” (Rev. XVII, 7–9ff.).

This was shown by Daniel: the fourth beast, which was greater than all the beasts and had that many horns (Dan. VII, 7).

16. But where he says there that a little horn arose and cast out three horns before it (ibid., 8)—[Note: [Col. 0844D] The words “and cast out three horns” are taken from the Remigius manuscript]—here he names seven kings, after those three had been expelled; and he indicates that the eighth itself is Antichrist, since it is one of the seven.

Therefore, insofar as one may conjecture, he either recalls the earlier kings who were more savage toward the Christian religion, [Note: [Col. 0844D] The older edition reads “in the Christian religion,” and the Remigius manuscript does not correct it. More recent editions put the phrase in the accusative.] or, after three of the ten have been destroyed, he means that seven will come who will themselves rage against the Church.

He plainly wants all the heretical Arians to be understood when he says: “These will fight against the Lamb, and the Lamb will conquer them” (Dan. VII, 14). [Note: [Col. 0845D] This note is printed at the foot of column 845, but its callout letter, *e*, does not appear in the text. The Remigius manuscript reads *Ad persecutionem* (“for persecution”).] For they fight by blowing upon and rebaptizing the members of the Lamb, whom Christ had already consecrated with his own blood. But the Lord says: “No one was lost except the son of perdition” (John XVII, 12).

Accordingly, some wish the eighth [Note: [Col. 0845D] The Remigius manuscript reads “king”; the Lugdunense and Cologne editions read “kingdom”; the Lovaniense and Duacense editions read “of kings.”] king whom he calls Antichrist to be understood as Nero, so that he himself may be the beast that was and is not and is to come again.

But whether he assumes Nero’s bodily form and appearance and appears in it—as, conversely, the holy angel in the Book of Tobit assumed the appearance and likeness of Azariah, the great Ananias (Tob. V, 8)—or whether Antichrist appears in the likeness of someone else, the prophet Daniel testifies that he will nevertheless possess Nero’s lust, depravity, savagery, and character; these matters are to be demonstrated in the following chapter.

## CHAPTER IX

Concerning the character of Antichrist. The prophecy to be fulfilled.

[Col. 0845B]

17. The prophet Daniel says that the angel told him: “The sons of the transgressors of your people will also exalt themselves in order to fulfill the vision” (Dan. XI, 14). And shortly afterward: “A contemptible and unworthy man will stand in the place of the kingly dignity, and in a few days he will be crushed, not in anger or in battle. And the king will act according to his will; he will be exalted and magnified against every god, and he will speak grand things against the God of gods, and he will prosper until wrath is completed; for the decree has been carried out. He will pay no regard to the God of his fathers, and he will be in the desires of women; and he will honor a god whom his fathers did not know, and he will establish the god *Moazi* in his place” (ibid., 20ff.).

Here it is shown that Antichrist will come from the Jews, from the tribe of Dan, which is still in Persia, in accordance with the prophetic blessing of the patriarch Jacob, who said: “Dan shall judge his people like the other tribes. Let Dan be a serpent in the way, a horned serpent on the path, biting the horse’s hooves so that its rider falls backward” (Gen. XLIX, 16–17).

Immediately afterward he shows that the true Christ the Lord will come, saying: “I shall await your salvation, O Lord” (ibid., 18).

The Lord also testified to this in the Gospel passage quoted above, saying to the Jews: “I have come in my Father’s name, and you did not believe me; another will come in his own name, and him you will believe” (John V, 43). [Note: [Col. 0845D] The Remigius manuscript reads “he will come … and him you will believe.”]

Paul, reproving these transgressors of the Law, shows that they will believe Antichrist: “Because they did not receive the love of the truth so that they might be saved, therefore God will send them a working of error, so that they may believe the lie and all may be judged who did not believe the truth but consented to iniquity” (2 Thess. II, 10–11). [Note: [Col. 0845D] The Remigius manuscript reads “who do not believe.”]

It must certainly be noted that all these things will come after the beast—that is, after the kingdom in which the woman sits, drunk with the blood of the saints, has been removed. [Note: [Col. 0845D] The Remigius manuscript reads “in which the woman sat.”] We who believe these things leave them for our successors to see.

## CHAPTER X

Concerning the persecutions of Antichrist. The prophecy to be fulfilled.

18. In Daniel’s vision the angel says concerning Antichrist: “His heart is against the holy covenant.” And there: “Arms shall arise from him and profane the sanctuary of strength; they shall remove the continual sacrifice and set up the abomination of desolation, and the impious shall counterfeit the covenant deceitfully.”

Here too he signifies the Arians as the forerunners of Antichrist. “But the people,” he says, “who know their God will prevail, and the learned among the people will be very numerous. [Note: [Col. 0845D] The Remigius manuscript reads “and they will teach many.”] And they will fall by the sword, by flame, by captivity, and by plunder for days. When they fall, they will be raised up by a little help, and many will join themselves to them deceitfully. And some of the learned will fall, so that they may be refined, chosen, and purified until the appointed time” (Dan. XI, 30–31ff.).

Again there: “At that time Michael will arise, the great prince who stands for the sons of your people; and there will come a time such as has not been since the beginning, from the time when nations began to exist, until that time. And at that time all your people who are found written in the book of life will be saved” (Dan. XII, 1ff.).

The Lord confirms these things in the Gospel: “When you see the abomination of desolation, which was spoken of by Daniel the prophet, let the one who reads understand” (Matt. XXIV, 15; Dan. IX, 27). And again: “In those days there will be tribulation and distress such as has not been from the beginning. And unless God had shortened those days, no flesh would have been saved; but for the sake of the elect those days will be shortened” (Matt. XXIV, 21–22).

John also testifies in the Apocalypse: “Power was given to the beast to speak great things, and it opened its mouth in blasphemy against God, to blaspheme his name and his tabernacle. And power was given to it to make war against the saints and to conquer and kill them. And power was given to it over every tribe, language, and nation, and all who are not written in the book of life of the Lamb [Note: [Col. 0845D] The Remigius manuscript reads “which has existed from the origin.”] who was slain from the foundation of the world will worship it” (Rev. XIII, 2ff.).

Here too the martyrdoms of Christ the Lord shine forth, so that just as his first advent supplied the number of thousands of infants, his second may complete the number of the elect. [Note: [Col. 0846D] The printed editions read “the number”; the Remigius manuscript, better, reads “the number” in the accusative.]

## CHAPTER XI

Concerning the pride of Antichrist. The prophecy to be fulfilled.

[Note: [Col. 0846D] The printed editions read “the promise”; the Remigius manuscript reads “the prophecy.”]

19. The prophet Ezekiel says: “Your heart was lifted up, and you said, ‘I am God, I sit in the seat of God, in the heart of the sea,’ although you are a human being and not God. And you set your heart as though it were the heart of God” (Ezek. XXVIII, 2).

The apostle Paul also says: “When the defection comes first and the man of sin, the son of perdition, is revealed, he will exalt himself above everything called God or worshiped, so that he sits in the temple of God, displaying himself as though he were God” (2 Thess. II, 3–4).

And the Lord says in the Gospel: “When they tell you, ‘Behold, here is the Christ; behold, there,’ do not believe” (Mark XIII, 21). [Note: [Col. 0846D] The Remigius manuscript reads “do not believe”; the printed editions read “do not go after them.”]

And in the Apocalypse of John: “I saw a beast rising from the earth; it had two horns like those of a lamb, and it spoke like a dragon” (Rev. XIII, 11). And shortly afterward: “It performed great signs, so that it even made fire descend from heaven to earth in the sight of human beings, and it deceived those who dwell on the earth because of the signs that were granted it to perform” (ibid., 13–14).

Here let the curious beware, especially the Jews. The Jews seek signs, as the Apostle says, while the Greeks seek wisdom (1 Cor. I, 22). Hence some conjecture that Antichrist will sit in Solomon’s temple, or that he will exalt himself through signs by which he will be believed to be Christ. For it has also been shown that he will have heralds of his falsehood, since it is said that he will have two horns like those of a lamb.

John also says in the Apocalypse: “I saw three unclean spirits coming from the mouth of the dragon, from the mouth of the beast, and from the mouth of the false prophet, like frogs; for they are spirits of demons, performing signs. They will go out to the kings of the whole world, to gather them for battle on that great day of the Almighty” (Rev. XV, 13–14).

For what is said in Daniel, “*Examina* [swarms] shall arise from him” (Dan. XI, 31), [Note: [Col. 0846D] Thus read the printed editions and the Remigius manuscript. But in the Greek text of the Septuagint, which our author follows, the reading is *σπέρματα* (“seeds”); this word could easily have been altered by a less careful copyist into the different word *examina*.] is here plainly expressed by the statement that three unclean spirits will go out like his heralds, as though toward the three parts of the world—that is, Asia, Europe, and Africa—and will persuade people through signs that Antichrist himself is Christ. But that he is not Christ will be demonstrated by what follows.

## CHAPTER XII

Concerning proving that Antichrist is not Christ. The prophecy to be fulfilled.

20. What has been said above makes clear with what pride Antichrist will come. His coming, therefore, will not be humble, as every prophecy resounds concerning Christ, Isaiah saying: “In his humiliation judgment was taken away; but who will declare his generation? For his life will be taken from the earth” (Isa. LIII, 8). [Note: [Col. 0847D] The Remigius manuscript reads “his birth … who has declared it? For he is taken away,” and so forth.]

He will not be led like a sheep to the slaughter (ibid., 7), that is, to the Passion, as the Gospels and prophecies testify that Christ was led. He will not give his cheek to the one who strikes him, nor, when receiving spittle and blows, will he remain silent (Lam. III, 30)—things that we believe were done to Christ, as every prophecy foretold them.

He will not give his back to scourges, nor will he be satisfied with reproaches (ibid.); that Christ fulfilled these things is proclaimed by the whole Gospel and by prophecy.

His garments will not be divided, nor will anyone cast lots for his tunic—something that the Gospels and prophecies testify happened to Christ’s clothing (John XIX, 23; Ps. XXI, 19). [Note: [Col. 0847D] The Remigius manuscript adds “and the Gospel also bears witness.”]

He will not be crucified, nor will he receive gall [Note: [Col. 0847D] The Remigius manuscript reads “or vinegar.”] and vinegar—things that the Gospels and prophecies say Christ received (Matt. XXVII, 34; Ps. LXVIII, 22).

His side will not receive a spear, nor will there be wounds from nails in him—wounds that the Gospels and prophecies testify were present in Christ even after the resurrection (John XIX, 29; Ps. XXI, 17).

He will not redeem the world with his blood—something that every prophecy proclaims concerning Christ.

He will not die and rise on the third day—things that the Gospels, the apostolic letters, and the prophecies testify Christ did (Matt. XXVII, 50; XXVIII, 6; 1 Cor. XV, 3–4; Hos. VI, 3).

He will not ascend into heaven, nor pour out the Holy Spirit upon the disciples in fiery tongues—things that the whole Gospel and prophecy proclaim Christ fulfilled.

Beyond these matters, the whole world itself is already a witness.

21. Therefore, after examining and considering these things, let those who will come after us understand that Antichrist is not Christ. The Apocalypse itself reveals his end: “The angel came and seized the dragon, the beast, and the false prophets. These were cast alive together into the pool burning with fire and sulfur, and they will be tormented there for ages of ages” (Rev. XX, 2, 10).

This will be the end of the devil, his angels, and those human beings who, under the mark and sign, [Note: [Col. 0847D] The Remigius manuscript reads “of his fellowship.”] passed over into his fellowship. The prophets Daniel and Ezekiel also testify concerning his end.

In these matters that have been stated, those who will then exist will do well to attend to prophecy as to a lamp in a dark place, until the day that is to come dawns in the hearts of believers (2 Pet. I, 19). The other final signs that are to come will be demonstrated in what follows.

## CHAPTER XIII

[Note: [Col. 0847D] The Remigius manuscript has “Concerning the sending.”]

Concerning the sending of Elijah and Enoch. The promise to be fulfilled.

[Col. 0847D]

22. In the prophet Malachi: “Behold,” he says, “the Lord declares: I will send you Elijah the Tishbite before the great and manifest day of the Lord comes; he will turn the heart of the father to the son, and the heart of a man to his neighbor, lest, when I come, I strike the earth utterly” (Mal. 4:5–6). For these prophets will turn the hearts of the fathers toward their sons, so that they may show what the patriarchs or prophets said about Christ who was to come in humility, proving that Antichrist is not Christ.

[Note: Col. 0847D. The Remigius manuscript reads “evidently.”]

The Apocalypse of John shows this still more clearly: “I will give power,” says the Lord, “to my two witnesses, and they will prophesy for 1,260 days, clothed in sackcloth. These are the two olive trees and the two lampstands standing before the Lord of the earth” (Apoc. 11:3–4). And shortly afterward: “They have power to shut heaven, so that no rain may fall during the days of their prophecy. And they have power over all waters, to turn them into blood, and to strike the earth with every plague, whenever they wish” (ibid. 6).

[Note: The printed editions read “will have”; afterward, the Remigius manuscript reads “to shut.”]

Behold, here too there is a threefold division of witnesses. Against Pharaoh, two witnesses of God were sent—Moses and Aaron—and two magicians of Pharaoh, Jannes and Jambres, resisted Moses (Exod. 5:1; 2 Tim. 3:8); they perished together with their king. Against Nero there were two, the apostles Peter and Paul; on the opposing side, Simon Magus, who destroyed himself and deceived Nero. Against Antichrist there will be two, the prophets Enoch and Elijah, against whom three false prophets of Antichrist will arise (Apoc. 16:13). One more is therefore present here, because one was lacking above, so that the number six may be completed from both sides, on account of the six days of creation established at the beginning, and the six angels sounding trumpets and bringing an equal number of plagues upon the world (Apoc. 8:6; 9:1 ff.). Thus the seventh signifies the end of labors and the rest of the saints, like the seventh day, which will have morning only and no evening.

[Note: The Remigius manuscript reads, “for it will not have evening.”]

This Sabbath rest divinity itself commends for observance by every commandment, so that, freed from every evil work, we may stand in the morning (Ps. 5:5), and contemplate him who crowns all with mercy and compassion (Ps. 102:4), judging justly and condemning no one unjustly. But Tyconius wrote much about these matters. Daniel the prophet also commends the consummation and completion of the times—three years and six months, which are called 1,260 days and make forty-two months—not only the Apocalypse of John (Apoc. 12:6), but Daniel as well (Dan. 12:11; 11:2): during these months, Gog and Magog—as some have said, the Goths and Moors, the Getae and Massagetae—will be able to trample the holy city, as the heretics, especially the Arians who were then very powerful, suppose.

[Note: The Lyon and Louvain editions read “which, as it is thought by heretics, and especially by the Arians, who were then very powerful, will be able to trample the holy city”; the Remigius manuscript reads “as it is thought … will be able.” The Cologne and more recent editions read “as it was thought … who were then very powerful.” The sense appears to be that this was written by Tyconius at the time when the Arians were especially powerful.]

As for Gog and Magog (Ezek. 39:1, 6), some have said that these are the Goths and Moors, the Getae and Massagetae, through whose savagery the devil himself now lays waste to the Church, and at that time they will persecute it more severely.

[Note: The Remigius manuscript reads “persecutes”; perhaps the future “will persecute.”]

They will also cause the perpetual sacrifice to cease. For this reason the Lord admonishes us, saying: “I am coming soon. Blessed is the one who keeps watch and preserves his garments, lest he walk naked” (Apoc. 16:15). What garments must be preserved, the following chapter will show.

## CHAPTER XIV. On the Garment to Be Preserved by Christians

[Note: The Remigius manuscript reads: “The promise to be fulfilled concerning the garment to be preserved.”]

**The Prophecy to Be Fulfilled**

23. The apostle Paul says: “As many of you as were baptized in Christ have put on Christ” (Gal. 3:27). And the Lord says in the Gospel: “The one who has been washed has no need to wash, except his feet, for he is wholly clean” (John 13:10). Therefore everyone rebaptized by heretics has either voluntarily lost his garment, Christ, or, failing during persecution, loses the clothing he possessed.

[Note: The Remigius manuscript reads “In the Passion.”]

While there is still time, let the one who has been stripped return in repentance, naked and dispossessed, to the merciful Father, who commands that the returning prodigal son be given back his first robe and, at the same time, the ring of dignity (Luke 15:22). Whoever still desires to be fed by the crooked arguments of heretics, as though by the pods of pigs (ibid. 15), should remember the bread and the father; let him flee his robbers and despoilers, and let him be ashamed that the Son of God has become the slave of Antichrist.

[Note: The Remigius manuscript reads *torturiosis*; if rendered in Latin, the word would be understood as derived from *torquere*, “to torture.”]

Let him return willingly or with contrition, so that he may be clothed and not be judged when displayed naked.

[Note: The Remigius manuscript adds: “Let them be ashamed of Christ [perhaps, ‘the Christian’] who has been stripped.”]

[Note: Col. 0849D. The Remigius manuscript adds: “Let them be ashamed of Christ [perhaps, ‘the Christian’] who has been stripped.”]

These are the things that the witnesses of God will do for them together with the prodigal sons.

[Note: Col. 0849D. The Remigius manuscript reads, “These things for them.”] In these events Elijah and Enoch will complete their martyrdom (Apoc. 11:5, 10), as the authority of the following chapter relates.

## CHAPTER XV. On the Passion of Elijah and Enoch

**The Prophecy to Be Fulfilled**

24. In the Apocalypse of John it is said: “When they have completed their martyrdom, the beast that ascends from the abyss will make war against them, conquer them, and kill them; and their bodies will lie in the street of that great city which is spiritually called Sodom and Egypt, where their Lord was also crucified” (Apoc. 11:7–8).

[Note: Col. 0849D. The Remigius manuscript reads “ascends.”]

This street is the conscience of all the ungodly, who in the world applaud the death of the saints because they think they have been rid of exceedingly bitter enemies. For this reason they will not allow their bodies to be placed in tombs.

[Note: The Remigius manuscript reads “in tombs”; the printed editions read “in the tomb.”]

For these two prophets tormented those who dwell upon the earth (ibid. 9–10). When they have been killed and the ungodly say, “Peace and security,” sudden destruction will overtake them, like labor pains upon a woman with child, and they will not escape. For, as the apostle Paul says, “the day of the Lord will come like a thief in the night” (1 Thess. 5:2–4).

## CHAPTER XVI. On the Resurrection of Elijah and Enoch

[Note: The Remigius manuscript reads: “The promise concerning the resurrection of Elijah and Enoch.”]

**The Promise to Be Fulfilled**

25. The Apocalypse of John says: “After three and a half days, the spirit of life from God entered them, and they stood upon their feet” (Apoc. 11:11). I think the apostle Paul spoke of them when he said: “And the dead in Christ will rise first” (1 Thess. 4:15). The three and a half days therefore correspond to three years and six months, during which Antichrist will have power. When these have been completed, Elijah and Enoch will ascend into heaven before the eyes of their enemies and go to meet Christ, the true King and Judge, when he comes (Apoc. 11:12). He will kill Antichrist and all his followers with the breath of his mouth (2 Thess. 2:8), so that he himself may reign in the house of Jacob, of whom it was said: “His kingdom will have no end” (Luke 1:32–33; Mic. 4:7).

## CHAPTER XVII. On the Coming of the Glory of the Son of God and of Man

[Note: The Remigius manuscript reads: “Concerning the coming,” and so forth.]

**The Promise to Be Fulfilled**

26. The prophet David says: “God will come openly, our God, and he will not be silent. Fire will burn before him, and a mighty storm will rage around him” (Ps. 49:3). The prophet Malachi also says: “Woe to those who desire the day of the Lord! Why do you desire it?” (Amos 5:18). Again: “The Lord whom you seek will suddenly come to his temple, and the Angel of the covenant whom you desire. Behold, he will come,” says the Lord. “And who will endure his coming? Or who will withstand his appearance? For he will enter like a refiner’s fire” (Mal. 3:1 ff.).

Isaiah also says: “Behold, the day of the Lord will come like fire, and his chariots like a storm, to repay vengeance in wrath and recompense in a flame of fire” (Isa. 66:15). The Lord likewise says in the Gospel: “For just as lightning comes out from the east and appears as far as the west, so will be the coming of the Son of Man” (Matt. 24:27). And again: “The sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light; the stars will fall from heaven, and the powers of heaven will be shaken. Then they will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds with great power and glory” (ibid. 29–30).

27. The Apocalypse of John also bears witness, saying: “The sun became black like a sackcloth of hair, and the moon became like blood, and the stars of heaven fell to the earth, just as a fig tree shaken by a great wind drops its unripe figs. The sky vanished like a scroll when it is rolled up, and every mountain and island was moved from its place. The kings of the earth and the greatest officials, the rich and the powerful, slaves and free persons, hid themselves in caves and among the rocks of the mountains, saying to the mountains and rocks: ‘Fall upon us and hide us from the face of the Father who sits upon the throne and from the wrath of the Lamb, because the great day of their wrath has come. And who will be able to stand?’” (Apoc. 6:12 ff.).

The apostle Paul also says: “The Lord himself will descend from heaven with a command, with the voice of an archangel, and with the trumpet of God” (1 Thess. 4:15). The Sibyl likewise acknowledges this, among other things, saying:

The sun’s radiance is taken away, and the choir of stars perishes;

The heaven will be rolled up; the moon’s brightness will vanish.

Then the trumpet from the lofty sphere will send down a mournful sound,

Lamenting the wretched crime and varied sufferings.

And the earth, splitting open, will reveal Tartarus’ chaos.

[Note: Our editions read *luminaris*, which is contrary to the laws of the verse. We have corrected it from Augustine, *City of God* 18.23.]

[Note: The printed editions of Prosper read “releases”; and below, “showed.” We have corrected these readings from the book of Augustine cited immediately above.]

28. I have omitted many necessary testimonies from the individual chapters, considering the limits of the work undertaken. Thus the coming of the Son of God brings joy to the good but destruction to the wicked. Now, while we are alive and there is time for correction, let us change our conduct and our habits.

The resurrection of the dead follows.

## CHAPTER XVIII. On the Resurrection of the Flesh

[Note: The Remigius manuscript reads: “On the resurrection.”]

**The Promise to Be Fulfilled**

29. The prophet Ezekiel: “The Lord said to me: Son of man, prophesy over these bones and say: Thus says the Lord: Behold, I will bring you out of your graves, and I will put sinews upon you, and lay flesh upon you, and stretch skin over you. I will put my spirit in you, and you will live, and you will know that I am the Lord” (Ezek. 37:4 ff.).

Isaiah also says: “The dead will rise, and those who are in the tombs will be raised” (Isa. 26:19). And the Lord himself says in the Gospel: “The hour is coming when all who are in the tombs will hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who have done good will come forth to the resurrection of life, while those who have done evil will come forth to the resurrection of judgment” (John 5:25).

Paul also testifies that this will happen in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet: “The trumpet will sound,” he says, “and the dead will rise incorruptible, and we will be changed” (1 Cor. 15:52).

[Note: Col. 0850D. The Remigius manuscript reads: “The trumpet will sound … and the dead will rise.”]

The Apocalypse likewise says: “The sea gave up the dead who were in it; likewise Death and Hades” (Apoc. 20:13).

Here the question arises which is put forward by the mouths of foolish pagans: How will those rise whose corpses were eaten by beasts and wild animals, and those animals themselves were consumed by other beasts, birds, and dogs? They do not understand that everything created from the earth returns to the same material when dissolved, and that it is easy for the Creator’s power to restore from it again what once existed—he who was able, among other things, first to form from it a human being who did not exist.

[Note: The Remigius manuscript reads: “If this troubles anyone.” The passage that follows, concerning what is written in the first psalm, is supplied from the same manuscript. In the printed editions only this appeared: “If anyone is troubled by the fact that the wicked do not rise in judgment, let him understand,” and so forth.]

If anyone is troubled by what is written in the first psalm—that the wicked do not rise in judgment (Ps. 1:5)—let him understand that they rise not for judgment but for punishment, in accordance with the Lord’s sentence: “Whoever does not believe,” he says, “has already been judged” (John 3:18).

The Sibyl also acknowledges this:

Thus the souls will be present with the flesh, whom he himself judges.

[Note: The Remigius manuscript reads “the souls from the flesh”; in Augustine it later reads “whom he himself judges.”]

When all have risen, judgment follows.

## CHAPTER XIX. On the Judgment of Christ the Lord

[Note: The Remigius manuscript reads: “On the judgment.”]

**The Promise to Be Fulfilled**

30. The prophet David says: “The heavens will proclaim his righteousness, for God is judge” (Ps. 49:6). Again: “He summoned heaven above and the earth, so that he might judge his people” (ibid. 4). Again: “He himself will judge the world in righteousness” (Ps. 95:13).

The Lord confirms this in the Gospel: “When the Son of Man comes in his glory, all the nations will be gathered before him, and he will separate them from one another, as a shepherd separates sheep from goats. He will place the sheep at his right hand, but the goats at his left. Then he will say to those at his right hand: ‘Come, blessed of my Father, receive the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world. For I was hungry and you gave me food’” (Matt. 25:31 ff.), together with the other works of mercy, in which there is a great sacrifice cleansing every sin, as the Lord himself says: “I desire mercy rather than sacrifice” (Matt. 9:13).

But to those on the left he will say: “Go into the eternal fire prepared by my Father for the devil and his angels. For I was hungry,” he says, “and you did not give me food” (Matt. 25:41–42), and similarly the other deeds belonging to the punishments of cruelty, which plunge a person into destruction and ruin (1 Tim. 6:9), when the greedy do not feed Christ who is hungry in the poor, who says: “As long as you did not do it for one of the least of mine, you did not do it for me” (Matt. 25:45).

The sentence of the Judge then follows between the two groups: “The wicked,” it is said, “will go into eternal burning” (ibid. 46).

31. The apostle Paul also testifies to these things: “We will all stand before the tribunal of Christ, so that each may receive according to what he has done through the body, whether good or evil” (2 Cor. 5:10).

The Apocalypse of John says: “I saw the dead, great and small, standing before the throne of God. Then books were opened, and another book was opened, which is the book of the life of each person; and the dead were judged from the things written in the books, according to their deeds” (Apoc. 20:12–13).

The opened books are the consciences of individuals. The other book, which contains the deeds of everyone, is the justice of God, bringing everything into the light.

[Note: Col. 0851D. The printed editions read “Concerning whom.”]

Concerning it Paul says: “Until the Lord comes, who will bring to light the things hidden in darkness and disclose the intentions of the heart; then each person will receive praise from God” (1 Cor. 4:5).

The Apocalypse of John concludes: “Death and Hades were thrown into the lake of fire; and whoever was not found written in the book of life was thrown into the lake of fire” (Apoc. 20:14–15), where they will be tormented forever and ever (ibid. 10; Isa. 66:24).

Isaiah likewise says: “Their worm will not die, and their fire will not be extinguished, and they will remain until the sight of all flesh is satisfied.”

[Note: The Remigius manuscript reads: “Their worms will not die, and their fire will not be extinguished, and they will be a spectacle to all flesh.”]

[Note: We have restored this passage from the book of Augustine cited so often above. In our printed editions it read: “The Sibyl acknowledges this, then exposing hidden deeds: Who will speak of secrets?

And God has opened hearts to the light;

Then there will also be mourning, and all will gnash their teeth.

And shortly afterward:

And before this Lord the kings will stand together.

Fire and a stream of sulfur will fall from heaven.”

The printed text attributed to the author of this book what had been quoted from the Sibyl and violated the laws of meter.]

The Sibyl also acknowledges this:

Then each person, exposing hidden deeds, will speak.

He will reveal secrets, and God will open hearts to the light.

Then there will be mourning, and all will gnash their teeth.

And shortly afterward:

And before this Lord the kings will stand together.

Fire and a stream of sulfur will fall again from heaven.

After this, it follows that certain faithful persons and the elements themselves will be purified through purifying fire.

## CHAPTER XX. On Purifying Fire

[Note: The Remigius manuscript reads “purgatorial fire.”]

**The Promise to Be Fulfilled**

32. The prophet David: “All things will grow old like a garment; and like a cloak you will change them, and they will be changed, but you are yourself the same” (Ps. 101:27–28). Again, he says: “You tested us by fire, as silver is tested” (Ps. 65:10). And again: “We passed through fire and water, and you brought us into refreshment” (ibid. 12).
